topics.label: Lecture opening and introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and frames expectations for the session.

topics.label: Foundations, nomenclature, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental concepts, naming rules, and core C3 activation mechanism underlying the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream pathways that recognise pathogens and drive C3 activation to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes executed by complement activation to destroy and clear pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic or acquired deficiencies in specific complement proteins result in distinct clinical disease manifestations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how pathogens subvert and resist complement-mediated immunity, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
